newsitem.title: JORDAN: Foreign share of Jordanian stock turnover 21 pct.
newsitem.headline: Foreign share of Jordanian stock turnover 21 pct.

text.p: Foreign investors bought and sold shares worth 19 million dinars ($26.8 million) in the Amman stock exchange last month, accounting for 21 percent of January turnover, figures released by the exchange showed on Tuesday.
Non-Jordanian Arab institutional and individual investor trading comprised 14 percent of January's total turnover, with seven percent attributed to funds from outside the region, the figures showed.
Foreign fund buying totalled 1.3 million dinars, with net purchases surpassing sales.

No comparison figures were provided but Jordanian investment managers have said foreign-based Middle East funds, which list Jordan as a main component, and global funds have been increasing their activity since December especially on blue-chips.

Global funds' stake on the bourse stood at end of 1996 at just 1.5 percent of a total market capitalisation of 3.5 billion dinars against a 33 percent held by non-Jordanian Arab investors. The rest is held by the government and Jordanian investors.
Trade by non-Jordanians, both Arabs and foreign, was 18 percent of 1996 total turnover of 248 million dinars.
